newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Mass of Hutu refugees head for Rwanda border.
newsitem.headline: Mass of Hutu refugees head for Rwanda border.

text.p: A huge mass of Hutu refugees trudged through the east Zaire town of Goma on Friday heading for the Rwandan border after abandoning besieged Mugunga camp, witnesses said.
"There is a sea of people right up to the horizon," said Reuters photographer Peter Andrews.
"There could easily be 100,000 of them. They are walking back to Rwanda," he said.
The Hutu refugees are part of the 1.2 million scattered around eastern Zaire by a one-month rebellion.
Zairean rebels checked them for weapons and let them walk the few km (miles) to the Rwandan border at Gisenyi.
The exodus from Mugunga came after six hours of shelling around the sprawling camp on Thursday.
Thousands of armed Hutus in and around Mugunga -- ex-Rwandan soldiers and Interahamwe militiamen -- appeared to have lost their grip over the refugee rank-and-file.
The fighters, blamed for the 1994 genocide in Rwanda which targeted minority Tutsis, have tried to forcibly prevent ordinary refugees from returning to their homeland.
But the effort seemed to be failing, judging by the human tide heading to Rwanda on Friday morning.
Refugees told reporters the Rwandan fighters in the camps were fleeing after Thursday's bombardments, moving into the bush with their weapons.
The armed elements face execution or many years of imprisonment if they return to Rwanda and are found guilty of committing acts of genocide or crimes against humanity in 1994.
"The refugees don't look too bad but they are obviously tired from walking. There are many men among the women, children and old people," Andrews said by telephone from Goma.
